A budgeting app designed for a fixed salary isn't a budgeting app anymore. It's a museum exhibit.
A fixed monthly budget did not reflect the irregular-income situations this project set out to explore.
Open any major budgeting or finance app and the same silent assumption is baked into onboarding: enter your monthly income. One number, one date, done.
The starting concern was an onboarding flow that asks for a single monthly income. That assumption does not describe every earner, and it became the constraint I wanted this design to address.
For a huge and fast-growing share of earners, that assumption is simply wrong.
For the irregular-income users considered in this study, that assumption is a poor fit.
and no finance app currently tells them apart.
and need a clearer way to see that distinction.
Higher scores were built first.
Higher scores informed the proposed build order.

The design only means something if it can run — fast, and at the scale multi-source, real-time income tracking demands. The system is structured as five layers, client apps down to external integrations, each communicating only with the layer directly above and below it.

The following is the proposed architecture from the design phase, not a description verified against a deployed app. It groups responsibilities into client, gateway, services, data and external integrations. Provider capabilities, access arrangements and the final implementation still need to be checked.
Dockerized microservices behind an API gateway, deployed on AWS, built to scale horizontally
Proposed Dockerized services behind an API gateway on AWS; deployment and scaling are not verified
JWT-based sessions plus biometric login via Firebase Auth
Proposed session authentication with Firebase Auth; device biometric access needs a separate platform implementation
Razorpay for top-ups, transfers, and bill payments
Razorpay considered as a payment provider; individual use cases, eligibility and capabilities require confirmation
Account Aggregator framework (Setu / Finvu) — secure, consent-based access to multiple accounts
Account Aggregator providers such as Setu / Finvu considered for consent-based access; no live connection or provider relationship is established here
